subtopics.title: Autonomous Spending, the MPC and the MPS

questions.question: Autonomous consumption is:
options: Spending that does not depend on current income — financed by dissaving, borrowing, grants or family
The part of consumption that varies with income

questions.question: Income rises by R2 000 and consumption rises by R1 500. The MPC and MPS are:
In the consumption function C = C₀ + cY, the letter c stands for:
options: The marginal propensity to consume — the fraction of each EXTRA rand of income that is spent

questions.question: Why does the MPC tend to be higher for poorer households?
options: A household with little income spends essentially every additional rand, while a high earner banks a large share of a bonus — which is why the DESTINATION of an injection changes its power

questions.question: With an MPC of 0,8, an injection of R1 000 generates the series 1 000 + 800 + 640 + 512 + … which sums to:
The multiplier formula is:
The multiplier is LARGE when:
options: People spend a large share of each extra rand — that is, when leakages are small

questions.question: On the 45-degree diagram, shifting the aggregate spending line UP by the injection produces:
options: An equal horizontal and vertical movement
A movement along the spending line only
A HORIZONTAL movement in income larger than the vertical shift — and the ratio between them is the multiplier

subtopics.title: Working the Multiplier with Rand Figures

questions.question: Government spends an extra R6 billion and the MPC is 0,75. National income rises by:
National income rose by R30 billion after an injection of R7,5 billion. The MPC is:
With MPS 0,10, MPT 0,25 and MPM 0,15, the open-economy multiplier is:
Why does spending on local construction labour multiply further than spending on imported machinery?
options: The import leakage is smaller, so more of each rand stays in the domestic chain and becomes somebody else's income

subtopics.title: Leakages, Limits and the Reverse Gear

questions.question: The multiplier raises real OUTPUT rather than prices only if:
options: There is spare capacity — idle workers, land and factories able to meet the extra demand

questions.question: Exports fall by R5 billion in an economy with a multiplier of 2. National income:
options: Falls by R10 billion — the multiplier works downwards with equal force

questions.question: Automatic stabilisers such as progressive tax and unemployment insurance:
options: Increase the multiplier in a boom
Have no effect on national income
Shrink the DOWNWARD multiplier by keeping incomes and spending steadier than they would otherwise be

questions.question: The ACCELERATOR describes how:
options: Interest rates rise when government borrows
Tax revenue falls in a recession
Rising consumer demand induces firms to invest in new capacity — and that investment is itself an injection, which multiplies again

questions.question: The bricklayer receives R1 000, keeps R200 and spends R800. The R800 is:
options: The spaza owner's income — the rand becomes somebody else's earnings

questions.question: With a fifth kept back at every stop, R1 000 of road repairs raises the town's total income by:
The point of the six-pocket chain is that:
options: A rand does not stop when it is spent — it becomes somebody's income and goes round again

subtopics.title: Why the Chain Gets Shorter Each Time

questions.question: The three ways a slice of each rand steps out of the chain are:
If half of every rand steps out at each stop, R1 000 of road repairs adds:
"Who gets the money matters" because:
options: A rand given to a household with nothing is almost entirely spent, so the chain runs long; a rand given to a wealthy household is largely saved, so the chain runs short

questions.question: When a mine cuts shifts, "one closure empties several tills" because:
options: The chain runs in reverse — the lost wage costs the spaza a customer, the wholesaler an order and the barber a client

subtopics.title: What the Chain Means on Budget Day

questions.question: The three questions to ask of any new spending announcement are:
options: Is there spare capacity? How much leaks out? How long will it take?
Who announced it? Is it popular? Is it legal?
What is inflation? What is the repo rate? What is the rand worth?
Are exports rising? Are imports falling? Is the budget balanced?

questions.question: If the economy is already running flat out — or trains and power stations cannot carry more — extra spending mainly:
options: Raises PRICES, because the extra money chases the same quantity of goods

questions.question: "Buy local" is an economic argument because:
options: A smaller import leak means a longer chain and a bigger total effect on domestic income

questions.question: The fair objection a strong answer must mention is:
options: Where the money came from — borrowed funds must be repaid with interest, and heavy borrowing can push rates up so businesses build less
